learning_experiences: define the term, sin from the biblical perspective,
read Genesis 3:1-13 and write short notes on the origin of sin,
read Genesis 3: 14-19, 23, 4:6-12, Genesis 11:1-9 and make notes on the consequences of sin,
list the sins young people are likely to commit today,
discuss the causes of sin among young people today,
brainstorm on how to overcome sin, temptations and tempting situations as a young person,
brainstorm on moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations,
write the moral values and life skills on charts and display them in class,
make a prayer to God every day for grace to overcome temptations,
repent whenever you fall into temptations as guided by 1John 1:9
write 1John 1:9 on flashcards and meditate on it.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to consider the consequences of something before acting?

Responsibility: The learners decide to avoid sin, temptations and tempting places.
Respect: The learners accommodate each other’s views and take turns to read the Bible.
sub_strands.pcis:
Decision-making: The learners, in pairs, buzz on how to overcome sin, temptations and tempting situations.
Spiritual development: The learners make a prayer to God every day for grace to overcome temptations. They also meditate on 1 John 1:9.
sub_strands.links:
English: The learners read, debate, brainstorm and communicate effectively as they share personal experiences.
Social Studies: The learners brainstorm on moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations.

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the forbidden thing was some other food, not the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

example.question: What had God forbidden Adam and Eve to eat?
example.wrong_answer: The fruit of the tree of life
example.correct_answer: The fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil

misconceptions.cause: The learner has not read Genesis 2:17 closely and fills in any food.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The fruit of the tree of life" beside "The fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 2:16-17 and 3:6: the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
misconceptions.feedback: They ate the forbidden fruit.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God tempted Eve, instead of the serpent.

example.question: Who tempted Eve in the garden?

misconceptions.cause: God set the rule, so the learner thinks God set the trap.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:1 and James 1:13: the serpent tempted; God tempts no one.
misconceptions.feedback: The serpent tempted Eve.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the fall changed nothing, missing shame, pain, toil, broken relationships and being sent from the garden.

example.question: Name a consequence of the fall in Genesis 3.
example.correct_answer: They were sent out of the garden; work became toil and childbirth painful

misconceptions.cause: The learner does not link sin with loss.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nothing changed" beside "They were sent out of the garden; work became toil and childbirth painful" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List consequences in Genesis 3:14-24: shame, fear, pain, toil, broken relationships, death, sent from the garden.
misconceptions.feedback: They were sent out of Eden.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God sends temptations to make people fall.

example.question: According to James 1:13, does God tempt anyone to do evil?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, God tempts us to see if we fall
example.correct_answer: No: each person is tempted by his own evil desire

misconceptions.cause: The learner mixes testing (trials that strengthen) with tempting to sin.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, God tempts us to see if we fall" beside "No: each person is tempted by his own evil desire" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read James 1:13-14. Tell testing from tempting: God allows trials, but never pushes to sin.
misconceptions.feedback: God does not tempt anyone to sin. Temptation comes from our own desires, and God gives a way out.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Blames every sin on the devil, so the person is not responsible.

example.question: Juma steals and says "the devil made me do it". What does James 1:14 teach?
example.wrong_answer: The devil is fully to blame
example.correct_answer: Each person is tempted by his own desire and is responsible for his choice

misconceptions.cause: Blaming the devil avoids shame, as Adam blamed Eve.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The devil is fully to blame" beside "Each person is tempted by his own desire and is responsible for his choice" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Link with Genesis 3:12-13 (blaming) and James 1:14 (own desire). Own the choice and repent.
misconceptions.feedback: We cannot blame the devil for our choices. Each person is responsible and can ask God for help.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks some temptations are too strong to resist, so giving in is unavoidable.

example.question: What does 1 Corinthians 10:13 promise about temptation?
example.correct_answer: God will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear and will give a way out

misconceptions.cause: The learner has felt strong pressure and believes it cannot be resisted.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Some temptations cannot be resisted" beside "God will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear and will give a way out" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Corinthians 10:13 and plan a "way out" for three common temptations.
misconceptions.feedback: God gives a way out of every temptation. You can stand with his help.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks being tempted is already a sin, so there is no point resisting.

example.question: Is it a sin to be tempted?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, being tempted is already sin
example.correct_answer: No: Jesus was tempted and did not sin; sin is giving in

misconceptions.cause: A wrong thought feels as guilty as a wrong act.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, being tempted is already sin" beside "No: Jesus was tempted and did not sin; sin is giving in" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Hebrews 4:15: Jesus was tempted in every way, yet without sin.
misconceptions.feedback: Being tempted is not sin. Jesus was tempted too. Sin is giving in, and God helps us resist.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Forgets that Adam and Eve hid from God out of shame and fear, the first sign of a broken relationship.

example.question: What did Adam and Eve do when they heard God walking in the garden (Genesis 3:8)?

misconceptions.cause: The learner remembers the eating and the punishment, not what came between.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Ran to greet him" beside "Hid among the trees" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:8-10 and ask why they hid: shame and fear replaced friendship with God.
misconceptions.feedback: They hid from God among the trees. Sin brought shame and broke their friendship with God.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

learning_experiences: buzz on the meaning of the word, ‘redemption’ and share with the class,
brainstorm on how God demonstrated his love after the fall of mankind,
in turns read the following scriptures on God’s salvation plan; Genesis 3:15; Genesis 12:1-3, Isaiah 53:5-12, Isaiah 63:5, Galatians 1:3-5, Colossians 1:13- 15, 2 Peter 3:9,

take part in sharing God’s love through evangelization and acts of mercy at school and in the community,
read Ephesians 1:7 and reflect on God’s saving grace.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is God’s redemptive plan important to human kind?

skills.name: Say how God showed love after the fall and planned salvation
skills.mastery: The child says God made clothes for Adam and Eve (Genesis 3:21), promised that the woman's offspring would defeat the serpent (Genesis 3:15), and that Christians believe He sent Jesus to save people (John 3:16). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Sin and its consequences come before redemption. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
John 3:16, God's love in giving his Son. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Prophecies of the Messiah fulfilled in Jesus. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God abandoned Adam and Eve after the fall, missing that he made clothes for them (Genesis 3:21).

example.question: What did God do for Adam and Eve after the fall?

misconceptions.cause: The learner remembers only the punishment.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Left them without help" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:21: God made garments of skin and clothed them. Love even in judgement.
misconceptions.feedback: God made clothes for them.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks John 3:16 says God gave a new law or a new garden, instead of his only Son.

example.question: What does John 3:16 say God gave?

misconceptions.cause: The learner remembers "God so loved the world" and guesses the rest.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A new law" beside "His one and only Son" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Recite John 3:16 together and underline "his one and only Son".
misconceptions.feedback: God gave His only Son.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Does not see that redemption restores the broken relationship between people and God.

example.question: Why is redemption important after the fall?
example.wrong_answer: It only helps people become rich
example.correct_answer: It restores people to friendship with God

misconceptions.cause: The word redemption is new and abstract.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It only helps people become rich" beside "It restores people to friendship with God" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Explain redeem as "buy back"; read Galatians 4:4-5 and Romans 5:8.
misconceptions.feedback: Redemption restores people to God.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks people earn salvation by good works, missing God's grace.

example.question: According to Ephesians 2:8-9, how are people saved?
example.correct_answer: By grace through faith, as God's gift

misconceptions.cause: At school and home, rewards are earned.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "By doing enough good works" beside "By grace through faith, as God's gift" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Ephesians 2:8-10: saved by grace, created for good works. Works follow, they do not buy.
misconceptions.feedback: We are saved by God's grace through faith. Good works are our thankful answer.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

learning_experiences: read Genesis 11:24-32 and Genesis 12:1 and summarise key points,
brainstorm and share with the class the meaning of the word, ‘faith.’
share experiences of how they exercise faith in God,

discuss the importance of God’s promises to Christians today,
brainstorm on how they should apply God’s promises in their day-to-day lives
key_inquiry_questions: How do you apply God’s promises in your daily life?

misconceptions.error: Thinks God told Abram to stay in his country, missing "Go from your country".

example.question: What did God tell Abram to do?
example.correct_answer: Leave his country for a land God would show

misconceptions.cause: The learner thinks God would not ask someone to leave home.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Stay in his country" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 12:1: "Go from your country". Mark Ur, Haran and Canaan on a map.
misconceptions.feedback: God told him to leave his country.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Says God provided a lamb in place of Isaac, from Abraham's words in 22:8, instead of the ram of 22:13.

example.question: What animal did Abraham find to offer instead of Isaac (Genesis 22:13)?
example.correct_answer: A ram caught by its horns

misconceptions.cause: Abraham told Isaac "God himself will provide the lamb" (Genesis 22:8), so the learner expects a lamb.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A lamb" beside "A ram caught by its horns" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 22:8 and 22:13: Abraham said a lamb; God provided a ram caught by its horns.
misconceptions.feedback: God provided a ram.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Says Abraham doubted and refused.

example.question: How did Abraham respond to God's call?

misconceptions.cause: The learner expects anyone to refuse such a hard call.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He refused" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 12:4 and Hebrews 11:8: "Abram went"; by faith he obeyed.
misconceptions.feedback: Abraham obeyed.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God's promise to Abraham was mainly gold and wealth, missing descendants, land and blessing.

example.question: Which was a promise to Abraham?

misconceptions.cause: The learner links blessing with money.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Great wealth in gold only" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: List the promises of Genesis 12:2-3, 15:5, 17:8: great nation, many descendants, land, blessing to all nations.
misconceptions.feedback: God promised many descendants.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks only Abraham's family would be blessed, missing "all peoples on earth" (Genesis 12:3).

example.question: Who would be blessed through Abraham?

misconceptions.cause: Family blessings are what the learner knows.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only his family" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 12:3: "all peoples on earth will be blessed through you". Link to Galatians 3:8.
misconceptions.feedback: All families would be blessed.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God's promises to Abraham mean nothing to Christians today.

example.question: Why do Christians value God's promises?
example.correct_answer: They can trust God to keep them

misconceptions.cause: Old promises seem to belong to the past.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "They are useless" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Show that God kept his promises to Abraham; Christians trust the same God (2 Corinthians 1:20).
misconceptions.feedback: Christians trust God's promises.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Forgets that Abraham waited many years for Isaac, thinking the son came at once.

example.question: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born (Genesis 21:5)?
example.wrong_answer: Still young, soon after the call
example.correct_answer: A hundred years old, after waiting many years

misconceptions.cause: Stories are told quickly and the waiting is lost.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Still young, soon after the call" beside "A hundred years old, after waiting many years" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw a time line: called at 75, Isaac born at 100. Faith means waiting for God's promise.
misconceptions.feedback: Abraham was a hundred when Isaac was born. He waited twenty-five years in faith.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Forgets the sign of the stars and thinks God showed Abraham a rainbow.

example.question: What did God tell Abram to count to show how many descendants he would have (Genesis 15:5)?

misconceptions.cause: The rainbow is the covenant sign with Noah.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The colours of a rainbow" beside "The stars in the sky" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 15:5 at night if possible: count the stars. Rainbow belongs to Noah (Genesis 9).
misconceptions.feedback: God told Abram to count the stars: so many would his descendants be.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a covenant is a gift.

example.question: What is a covenant?

misconceptions.cause: God's promises are free, so the learner thinks a covenant is only a gift.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A free gift" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Explain covenant: a binding agreement with promises and duties. God promised; Abraham was to walk faithfully (Genesis 17:1).
misconceptions.feedback: A covenant is a binding agreement.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Gives the rainbow (Noah's covenant) as the sign of the covenant with Abraham instead of circumcision.

example.question: What was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham?

misconceptions.cause: The rainbow is the best-known covenant sign.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A rainbow" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Make two cards: Noah, rainbow (Genesis 9); Abraham, circumcision (Genesis 17:11).
misconceptions.feedback: Circumcision was the sign.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Gives Isaac, his son's name, as Abram's new name instead of Abraham.

example.question: What was Abram renamed?

misconceptions.cause: Isaac is the next name in the family.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Isaac" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 17:5: Abram becomes Abraham; Sarai becomes Sarah (17:15).
misconceptions.feedback: Abram became Abraham.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks every agreement is good if both people agree.

example.question: A group asks a youth to swear a secret oath to obey its leader in everything. Is it a good covenant because he agrees?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, he agreed, so it is good
example.correct_answer: No: a secret oath that demands total obedience to a leader against God's law is ungodly

misconceptions.cause: The learner thinks consent alone makes an agreement right.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, he agreed, so it is good" beside "No: a secret oath that demands total obedience to a leader against God's law is ungodly" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List marks of an ungodly covenant: secrecy, against God's law, harm, control, other powers. Test this oath against them.
misconceptions.feedback: An agreement is not good only because people agree. Secret oaths that go against God's law are ungodly.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks covenants are only in the Bible and none exist today.

example.question: Which of these is a covenant in modern life?
example.correct_answer: Marriage vows, or a signed work contract

misconceptions.cause: The word covenant is met only in Bible lessons.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "There are none today" beside "Marriage vows, or a signed work contract" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show a marriage certificate and an employment letter: binding promises with duties on both sides.
misconceptions.feedback: Covenants exist today: marriage vows, contracts and agreements between nations.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a covenant made in secret is safer because no one can interfere.

example.question: What is a warning sign of an ungodly covenant?
example.wrong_answer: It is open and others know about it
example.correct_answer: It must be kept secret, even from parents and the church

misconceptions.cause: Secrecy sounds like loyalty.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is open and others know about it" beside "It must be kept secret, even from parents and the church" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Ephesians 5:11-13: what is done in darkness is exposed by the light. Godly agreements can be known.
misconceptions.feedback: Godly agreements can be known and checked. Secrecy from parents and church is a warning sign.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a covenant can be judged good by how exciting or profitable it feels.

example.question: How should a Christian discern whether an agreement is godly?
example.wrong_answer: By how much money or excitement it brings
example.correct_answer: By testing it against God's word and seeking advice from trusted, godly people

misconceptions.cause: Quick gain is the loudest measure the learner sees.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "By how much money or excitement it brings" beside "By testing it against God's word and seeking advice from trusted, godly people" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 John 4:1 (test the spirits) and Proverbs 15:22 (plans succeed with many advisers).
misconceptions.feedback: Test every agreement against God's word and ask trusted, godly people for advice.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God's covenant asked nothing of Abraham.

example.question: What did God ask of Abraham in the covenant (Genesis 17:1)?
example.correct_answer: To walk before God faithfully and be blameless

misconceptions.cause: The learner hears only the promises.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nothing at all" beside "To walk before God faithfully and be blameless" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 17:1-2 and 17:9-10: God promised, and Abraham was to walk faithfully and keep the sign.
misconceptions.feedback: God asked Abraham to walk before him faithfully, and to keep the sign of circumcision.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Says Israel asked for a king because Samuel was young, instead of because he was old and his sons were corrupt.

example.question: Why did Israel ask for a king?
example.correct_answer: Samuel was old and his sons did not follow his ways

misconceptions.cause: The learner does not recall why Samuel's leadership was ending.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Samuel was young" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 8:1-5: Samuel was old; his sons took bribes; the people wanted a king like the nations.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 Samuel 8 gives this reason.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Samuel said a king would give the people gifts, instead of warning that he would take their sons, land and harvest.

example.question: What did Samuel warn a king would do?

misconceptions.cause: The learner expects a prophet to welcome the people's wish.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Give them gifts" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 8:11-18 and list what a king would take: sons, daughters, fields, a tenth.
misconceptions.feedback: Samuel warned the king would take their sons and land.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Israel wanted to be unlike other nations, when they asked to be like them.

example.question: What did Israel want, according to 1 Samuel 8:20?
example.wrong_answer: To be different from all other nations
example.correct_answer: To be like other nations, with a king to lead them

misconceptions.cause: The phrase "like the nations" is read the wrong way round.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "To be different from all other nations" beside "To be like other nations, with a king to lead them" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 8:5 and 8:20: they wanted to be like other nations, with a king to lead and fight.
misconceptions.feedback: They wanted a king like other nations.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Saul waited for Samuel at Gilgal, instead of offering the sacrifice himself.

example.question: What did Saul do at Gilgal?

misconceptions.cause: The learner thinks a king would obey the prophet.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Waited for Samuel" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 13:8-13: Saul did not wait and offered the burnt offering himself.
misconceptions.feedback: Saul offered the sacrifice himself.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Saul destroyed all the Amalekite flocks, when he spared the best against God's command.

example.question: What did Saul do with the best Amalekite flocks?

misconceptions.cause: Sparing the best sounds kind and wise.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Destroyed them" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 15:9, 22: "To obey is better than sacrifice". Partial obedience is disobedience.
misconceptions.feedback: Saul spared the best flocks.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God made Saul greater after his disobedience, instead of rejecting him as king.

example.question: What was the result of Saul's disobedience?

misconceptions.cause: Kings in stories usually keep their thrones.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God made him greater" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 15:23, 26: God rejected Saul as king; David was anointed (1 Samuel 16).
misconceptions.feedback: God rejected Saul as king.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Misses that asking for a king was a rejection of God as king.

example.question: What did God tell Samuel the people were really rejecting (1 Samuel 8:7)?

misconceptions.cause: The learner sees only a quarrel between the people and Samuel.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Samuel" beside "God as their king" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 8:7 and discuss why God, not Samuel, was rejected.
misconceptions.feedback: God told Samuel they had rejected God as their king, not Samuel.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks offering sacrifices pleases God more than obeying him.

example.question: What did Samuel tell Saul in 1 Samuel 15:22?
example.correct_answer: To obey is better than sacrifice

misconceptions.cause: Saul's excuse sounds religious, so the learner accepts it.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Sacrifice is better than obedience" beside "To obey is better than sacrifice" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Samuel 15:22 and ask: can a gift replace doing what God said?
misconceptions.feedback: Samuel said, "To obey is better than sacrifice." God wants obedience more than offerings.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.cause: Healed people often go home in the stories.

misconceptions.help: Explain a beggar's cloak was his bed and begging mat; throwing it aside showed eager faith.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the friends brought the man through the front door, instead of through the roof.

example.question: How did the friends bring the man to Jesus?

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Through the front door" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.

misconceptions.error: Thinks leisure means hard work, instead of free time after duties.

example.question: What is leisure?

misconceptions.cause: The learner confuses free time with chores done in free time.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Hard work" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Define leisure: free time after work and duties, for rest and good activities.
misconceptions.feedback: Leisure is free time.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Calls reading a misuse of leisure, linking it with school work.

example.question: Which is a misuse of leisure?

misconceptions.cause: Reading is linked with school work, so it feels like a chore.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Reading a book" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Sort activities: builds up (reading, sport, hobbies, serving) and pulls down (drugs, gambling, idleness).
misconceptions.feedback: Gambling and drugs are misuse.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks idling all day is a constructive use of leisure.

example.question: Which is a constructive use of leisure?

misconceptions.cause: Idling feels restful and harmless.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Idling all day" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read 2 Thessalonians 3:11 and Proverbs 6:9-11: idleness leads to trouble and want.
misconceptions.feedback: Sport and helping are constructive.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks no values are needed in leisure time because it is free time.

example.question: Which value helps a youth use leisure well?
example.wrong_answer: None: free time needs no rules

misconceptions.cause: Free time feels like time without rules.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "None: free time needs no rules" beside "Self-control and time management" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compile values and life skills for leisure: self-control, time management, responsibility, decision-making. Read Ephesians 5:15-16.
misconceptions.feedback: Even free time needs self-control and good choices. Make the most of every opportunity (Ephesians 5:15-16).
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.
